label: Vinyl dirt
clause: Lay vinyl dirt so the hop has a crate hiss without a stock name.

label: Dry booth mix
clause: Keep the vocal dry in the mix so the booth is glass.

label: Club loudness
clause: Push club loudness so the drop has competitive weight.

label: Sidechain pump
clause: Pump sidechain so the kick punches a hole in the pad.

label: Tape hiss
clause: Leave tape hiss so the lo-fi bed has air noise.

label: Analog warmth
clause: Warm analog-leaning so the midrange is round.

label: Digital clip
clause: Clip digital-small so the transients have a square edge.

label: Narrow radio
clause: Narrow the mix so it reads like a small radio without a platform name.

label: Wide chorus mix
clause: Widen the chorus so the hook is physically larger than the verse.

label: Mono low end
clause: Mono the low end so the sub is center.

label: No-verb vocal
clause: Withhold vocal reverb so the booth stays close.

label: Plate vocal
clause: Plate the vocal small so there is a metal room not a hall.

label: Parallel crush
clause: Crush a parallel bus so the drums have weight without losing transients.

label: Downsampled dirt
clause: Downsample dirt so the crunch is a bit-depth cousin.

label: Telephone band
clause: Telephone-band a throw so the ad-lib is small and mid.

label: Loud-quiet
clause: Contrast loud and quiet so the drop is a dynamic not just a filter.

label: Bus glue
clause: Glue the bus gently so the kit feels like one instrument.

label: Clean master
clause: Leave the master clean so loudness is not a smashed brick.

label: Speech duck
clause: Duck the bed under speech so the host always wins.

label: Bright sting
clause: Brighten a sting so two bars cut through a talk bed.

label: Drive-through instrumental lock
clause: Lock a live bass-set mix so the take stays instrumental, chest-heavy, and free of brass.

label: Drive-through DJ-shout lock
clause: Lock a live bass-set mix so a sparse DJ shout can sit without a rap verse or brass.
